summary: Iteration 11 — WhatsApp Inbox end-to-end verification. Wrote 17 pytest cases covering (1) verify handshake success/failure, (2) HMAC-SHA256 X-Hub-Signature-256 validation on POST /webhooks/whatsapp, (3) inbound message persistence + auto-link to WATH applicant (phone 9999900000 → application_no 12477667), (4) idempotency of duplicate wa_message_id, (5) admin GET /threads + /messages + PATCH /read, (6) POST send hitting the REAL Meta Graph API (now returns 200 with a real wamid), (7) RBAC (unauth 401/403 + student 403). Found and fixed a critical body-parsing bug: SendMessageIn Pydantic model was declared inside build_whatsapp_router() closure — FastAPI resolves annotations via module globals and could not find the class, so it silently degraded `req: SendMessageIn` to `Query(...)` and every POST returned 422 'Field required: query req'. Moved the class to module scope; POST /whatsapp/threads/{id}/messages now returns 200. UI verified: WhatsApp Inbox tab loads, thread list renders, WATH-linked App No 12477667 chip shows, ChatPane opens on click, wa-text-input+wa-send-btn triggers a successful POST (post-fix).

critical_code_review_comments: FIXED — CRITICAL: SendMessageIn Pydantic model was defined inside build_whatsapp_router() function. FastAPI+Pydantic v2 resolves annotations via typing.get_type_hints using MODULE globals; a class in a factory-function's local scope becomes an unresolved ForwardRef and FastAPI silently downgrades the parameter from Body → Query. Result: every POST /api/whatsapp/threads/{id}/messages returned 422 'Field required: query req' regardless of request body. Fix applied: moved SendMessageIn to module scope in whatsapp_inbox.py. Post-fix verified: send now returns 200 with a real Meta wamid.

whatsapp_inbox.py::_verify_signature raises 500 when APP_SECRET not configured but the POST /webhooks/whatsapp handler only enforces signature *if* APP_SECRET is configured — the 500 path inside _verify_signature is unreachable in practice, but keep it as defence-in-depth.

whatsapp_inbox.py::send_message logs `resp.status_code + err` on failure but re-raises HTTPException with only err.error.message — admin doesn't see the Meta error code (e.g. 131030). Consider surfacing `err.error.code` in the detail for better UX.

whatsapp_inbox.py::_persist_inbound auto-links contact to the FIRST scholarship_application with matching phone. If multiple apps share the same phone (parents applying for siblings) only one gets linked. Low priority — acceptable for MVP.
SendMessageIn.template_components has mutable default `[]` — Pydantic v2 handles this correctly (deep-copies defaults), so no shared-state bug, but style-wise `default_factory=list` is preferred.

rca of the issue: ORIGINAL user-reported symptom: 'WhatsApp Inbox not working — no conversations appear'. RCA: (a) inbox itself is fine — user simply hasn't subscribed the webhook in Meta yet, so no inbound events reach the server (threads array legitimately empty). (b) SEPARATELY discovered a CRITICAL latent bug in send_message: Pydantic model SendMessageIn was declared inside build_whatsapp_router() function scope. FastAPI's Body vs Query auto-detection relies on typing.get_type_hints(handler_fn) which searches the handler's module globals (not the enclosing factory function's locals). Since SendMessageIn wasn't in module globals, get_type_hints returned an unresolved ForwardRef; FastAPI then treated `req: SendMessageIn` as a Query dependency and every send request returned 422 {'loc':['query','req'],'msg':'Field required'}. Fix (verified): moved `class SendMessageIn(BaseModel)` out of build_whatsapp_router() to module scope in /app/backend/whatsapp_inbox.py. Reproduction confirmed both via TestClient with the actual module (422 before fix, 200 after) and via live cURL against the running preview URL (200 with a real Meta wamid returned). Reproduction script was `pytest backend/tests/test_iteration11_whatsapp.py::TestAdminThreadsAPI::test_send_message_hits_meta_gracefully -v`.
